title: What Happens When You Don't Drink Enough Water?
sources: NHS, 'Dehydration' ('Dehydration means your body loses more fluids than you take in'; symptoms: 'feeling thirsty', 'headache and feeling light-headed', 'dark yellow, strong-smelling pee', 'peeing less often than usual', 'feeling tired', 'a dry mouth, lips and tongue', 'sunken eyes'; it happens more easily if you have been in the sun or a hot environment too long, sweat a lot after exercising, or have a high temperature; drink fluids 'so that your pee is a pale colour'; call 999 or go to A&E if someone with signs of dehydration has blue, grey, pale or blotchy skin, lips or tongue, or is confused; voiced as 'Call emergency services' for the US-majority audience): https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/dehydration/

NHS, 'Water, drinks and your health' ('aim to drink 6 to 8 cups or glasses of fluid a day'; 'Water, lower-fat milk and lower-sugar drinks, including tea and coffee, all count as part of your daily intake'; aim for urine that is 'a clear pale yellow colour'): https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/eat-well/food-guidelines-and-food-labels/water-drinks-nutrition/

NIH NCBI StatPearls, 'Physiology, Antidiuretic Hormone' (ADH is made in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary; rising blood osmolality or low blood volume triggers it; it makes the kidneys reabsorb water, producing concentrated urine and conserving water during dehydration): https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK526069/

Tease (next video): Cleveland Clinic, 'Sleep inertia' (the groggy 'transitional state you experience when you aren't asleep … but definitely aren't awake yet either', usually 15 to 60 minutes; 'Resist the urge to hit the snooze button'): https://health.clevelandclinic.org/sleep-inertia

lines.text: What happens when you don't drink enough water?
Six to eight glasses a day. Does coffee count, or just water?
lines.caps: SIX TO *EIGHT | *GLASSES | A *DAY | DOES *COFFEE | *COUNT | OR JUST *WATER?

lines.text: Fall short, and your brain sends a water-saving hormone.
Your kidneys pull water back into your blood,
so your pee turns dark yellow and strong-smelling.
But here's the sneaky part: sweat, heat or fever drain you faster.
lines.caps: BUT *HERE'S | THE SNEAKY *PART | *SWEAT | *HEAT | OR *FEVER | DRAIN YOU *FASTER

lines.text: Ever get a headache and dry mouth at work?
Blotchy, grey skin or confusion? Call emergency services.
Tea and milk count too. Aim for pale yellow pee.
lines.caps: TEA AND *MILK | COUNT *TOO | AIM FOR *PALE | YELLOW *PEE
